name: Figma
look: Monochrome core with oversized pastel colour-block sections, pills as the only button shape, and mono eyebrows flagging taxonomy.

hero.title: Nothing great is made alone
hero.sub: A design tool that runs in the browser, so the file is a URL and the version everyone is looking at is the same one.

features.title: One file, everyone in it
features.sub: Multiplayer stopped being a feature the moment the file became a URL.

items.title: Multiplayer
items.body: Cursors, selection and edits in real time. No merge, no export, no 'final v3'.

items.title: Components
items.body: Build once and reuse, with variants and properties, updated everywhere at once.

items.title: Handoff built in
items.body: Developers open the same file and read spacing, tokens and generated code.

items.title: Prototyping
items.body: Wire flows and interactions in the same file as the design, testable on a device.

items.title: Design systems
items.body: Published libraries with versioning, so a token change is a reviewable release.

items.title: Browser native
items.body: No install, no sync client, no file that lives on one laptop.

showcases.title: The file is a URL
showcases.body: Once the file lives at an address, sharing it is sending a link and reviewing it is leaving a comment on the thing itself. The whole category of exporting flat images for feedback disappears.

showcases.title: Design systems as releases
showcases.body: A published library is versioned. Updating a component is a release consumers choose to take, with a diff, rather than a change that silently appears in everyone's file overnight.

gallery.title: COMMUNITY
gallery.sub: Files, plugins and templates published by the people who use them.

testimonial.quote: We stopped exporting PNGs for review, and about a week later realised nobody had asked which file was the current one since.
testimonial.name: Yuki Tanaka

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free for individuals. Paid per editor, not per viewer.

items.a: No. You pay per editor. Anyone can be invited to view and comment for free, which is what makes sharing work across a company practical.
Recently opened files are cached and editable offline, syncing when you reconnect. Opening a file you have never viewed needs a connection.
Yes, in an open format plus flat assets. Nothing is trapped, though the collaboration is obviously what you lose by leaving.
A publish creates a release with a diff. Consuming files choose when to accept it, so a token change never silently rewrites someone's work in progress.

cta.title: Open a file
cta.sub: Free to start, browser native, and nothing to install.

notes: The system core is monochrome — black and white carry every CTA, every body line and every footer link.
Oversized pastel colour-block sections define the narrative rhythm of a long page. They are sections, not cards.
The pill is the only button shape. There are no square buttons anywhere in this system.
The variable typeface is used at unusually fine weight increments, so the type reads as one voice flexing rather than a multi-weight family.
A mono face is reserved for category labels, eyebrows and captions — always uppercase with positive tracking, flagging taxonomy without competing with the display.
